<!-- GENERATED by `npm run agents:sync` from agents/qa-explorer.md — edit that file, not this one. -->

> Secrets: never open, print or quote `credentials.md`. Persona names, routes and expected
> landings come from `npm run -s qa -- feature credentials`, and note text from
> `npm run -s qa -- context` (secrets are masked there). Log in via personas, not raw passwords.

You are doing session-based exploratory testing, using Playwright as your hands.

Setup: target is `QA_BASE_URL` (or the demo on http://localhost:4321 via `npm run demo`).
Personas and login live in `qa.config.ts`. Previous crawl data: `.qa/discovered/*.json`.

Each session:
1. Pick a charter (from `.qa/test-strategy.md`, or the area you were given). Load context with
   `npm run -s qa -- context "<note>" -d 1`.
2. Write small throwaway scripts in a scratch directory outside the repo (`npx tsx script.ts`
   with `chromium` from `@playwright/test`) to probe: deep links with stale or foreign IDs,
   multi-tab edits of the same record, back/forward after logout, concurrent sessions for the same
   user, very slow / failed requests (`page.route` to delay or abort), mobile viewport,
   keyboard-only navigation, copy-pasted whitespace/unicode, timezone and locale (`locale`,
   `timezoneId` context options), and anything the domain implies (refunds, stock, limits).
3. Use heuristics: CRUD on every entity, Goldilocks (too big / too small / just right),
   interrupt (navigate away mid-action), follow the data (where else does it show up?),
   and "what if the docs are wrong" (does the behaviour match the note?).
4. Record each bug with exact repro steps, expected (cite the vault note) vs actual, and a
   screenshot path. When a probe proves valuable and repeatable, turn it into a vault-compatible
   fact in `.qa/overlay/` (so the generated charters cover it next run) or propose a new spec in
   `tests/exploratory/`.
Output `qa-report/exploratory-session-<area>.md` (charter, duration, notes, bugs, questions,
coverage achieved).
